  > **1. Missing references**
  > 
  > Datasets (provenance, as in the PPI paper's own data sections, which I read: arXiv 2301.09633, §3):
  > - `galaxies`: Willett, Lintott, Bamford, Masters, Simmons, et al., "Galaxy Zoo 2: detailed morphological classifications for 304,122 galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey", *MNRAS* 435(4):2835–2860, 2013, doi:10.1093/mnras/stt1458. (It is item 8 of the task's starter literature.)
  > - `forest`: Bullock, Woodcock, Souza Jr., Olofsson, "Satellite-based estimates reveal widespread forest degradation in the Amazon", *Global Change Biology* 26(5):2956–2969, 2020, doi:10.1111/gcb.15029. The predictions come from the tree-cover product: Sexton, Song, Feng, Noojipady, et al., "Global, 30-m resolution continuous fields of tree cover: Landsat-based rescaling of MODIS vegetation continuous fields with lidar-based estimates of error", *Int. J. Digital Earth* 6(5):427–448, 2013, doi:10.1080/17538947.2013.786146.
  > - `plankton`: Olson, Shalapyonok, Sosik, "An automated submersible flow cytometer for analyzing pico- and nanophytoplankton: FlowCytobot", *Deep Sea Research Part I* 50(2):301–315, 2003, doi:10.1016/S0967-0637(03)00003-7. Also Orenstein, Beijbom, Peacock, Sosik, "WHOI-Plankton: a large scale fine grained visual recognition benchmark dataset for plankton classification", arXiv:1510.00745, 2015 (taken from the PPI paper's reference list; not in Crossref).
  > - `alphafold`: also cite the predictions: Jumper, Evans, Pritzel, Green, et al., "Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold", *Nature* 596:583–589, 2021, doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2. Bludau et al. 2022 is the data.
  > - `ballots`: I know of no peer-reviewed source. The PPI paper only thanks the San Francisco Department of Elections for help finding it. Describe it as the `ppi-python` 0.2.3 example data (San Francisco special election, 2022) and cite the package version, not a paper.
  > - `census_*`: Ding et al. 2021 is right. The PPI paper uses California ACS records through folktables.
  > - `gene_expression`: Vaishnav et al. 2022, *Nature* 603:455–463, is right (61,150 yeast promoters).

Also Chatterjee, Guntuboyina, Sen, "On risk bounds in isotonic and other shape restricted regression problems", *Ann. Statist.* 43(4):1774–1800, 2015, doi:10.1214/15-AOS1324.
  > - Cross-fitting: Schick, "On asymptotically efficient estimation in semiparametric models", *Ann. Statist.* 14(3):1139–1151, 1986, doi:10.1214/aos/1176350055. This is the sample-splitting origin that DML builds on. Cite it next to Chernozhukov et al.

Statist.* 28(4):1026–1053, 2000, doi:10.1214/aos/1015956706. I confirmed the metadata and title only; I have not read it, so cite it for "model-assisted nonparametric regression estimators exist", nothing more specific.

Statist.* 29(5):1189–1232, 2001, doi:10.1214/aos/1013203451. `experiment-repo` knows the implementation actually used. Cite that library, not the paper, if it is not a Friedman-style GBM.

Items 2, 3 and 6 are confirmed. Items 1, 4 and 5 need corrections.
  > 
  > **1. Clip. Three corrections; the rest is confirmed.**
  > - "b* below one on the other seven" is wrong. `clip_real.csv` has b* = 1.375 (census_income), 1.152 (gene_expression) and **1.034 (alphafold)**. Six sets are below one: plankton 0.844, forest 0.897, ballots 0.977, census_education 0.976, galaxies 0.978, census_healthcare 0.985.
  >   - On alphafold λ* is above 1 only at n ≤ 100 (1.030 at n=30, 1.021 at n=100) and the formula's predicted width ratio is 0.999. The "7% wider at n=30" is the cost of estimating λ, not the clip.
  >   - Suggested wording: "b* is above one on gene_expression (1.15), census_income (1.38) and, marginally, alphafold (1.03; the formula predicts a clip effect under 0.1%); below one on the other six".
  > - "Within 0.031 of the measured ratio on the real sets" holds for n ≥ 100 only. The maximum is gene_expression n=100 (0.031); for n ≥ 300 it is 0.010. At n=30 it reaches 0.079 (gene_expression) and 0.123 (plankton). It is 0.004 or less on census_income at every n. Please add "n ≥ 100".
  > - "census_income unclipped coverage 0.87 to 0.92 at n ≤ 300" should read **0.79 to 0.92**: n=30 0.786, n=100 0.871, n=300 0.919.
  > - Confirmed:
  >   - b* = 1.15 and 1.38 as quoted.
  >   - Unclipped PPI++ is valid on census_income from n=1000 (Wilson upper limit 0.957; 0.945 at n=500).
  >   - λ̂ > 1 in 70.7% of draws at n=30 (gene_expression).
  >   - Unclipped/package width ratio is 0.955 and 0.977 on gene_expression at n=100 and 500, and 0.976 and 0.985 on census_income.
  >   - Synthetic sweep, formula vs measured: 0.0139 at n=300, 0.0042 at n ≥ 1000, 0.088 at n=100, 0.131 at n=30.
  >   - For 0 ≤ b ≤ 1 and n ≥ 100 the ratio is within 0.0129 of one; at n=30 it is at most 1.046.
  >   - Unclipped saving at n=100, N=10^4, σ=0.6: 4.0% (b=1.2) to 65.7% (b=2).
  >   - The 61 synthetic cells have R = 4000 to 8000.
  >   - The n=100 gene_expression figures (0.890, 0.896, 0.921, package coverage 0.949) are from `decomp.csv` (3000 replicates). They are a different run from `clip_real.csv` (5000 replicates, package coverage 0.940), so the two coverages differ by Monte Carlo error.
  > 
  > **2. Strongest valid baseline.** Yes, this is exactly `baseline_used` and `ratio_vs_valid_baseline` (`build_results.py`, "strongest valid PPI++ baseline").
  > - "Valid" for a baseline means the Wilson upper limit of its coverage is ≥ 0.95, as for every arm. The paired-with-PPI++ condition is not applied to baselines.
  > - The package is valid in 21 of 51 T1 cells and the unclipped PPI++ in 26. The rule picks "neither valid, narrower of the two" in 24 cells; 25 cells have both valid, 1 only the package, 1 only the unclipped.
  > - Counts confirmed: 38 / 12 / 1 against the package, 39 / 12 / 0 against the valid baseline, 51 T1 cells (plus 4 T2 rows).
  > 
  > **3. Break-even scoring.** Confirmed from `breakeven_summary.csv`.
  > - 11 bracketed: 3 in quad_n_sweep, 2 in shapes, 5 in stress, 1 in reference_grid. 9 are within a factor of 3; the miss is census_income_log (stress), and the real-grid miss is gene_expression. The real grid has 8 censored curves.
  > - The "stress" curves are the real pools with a monotone-transformed predictor, not synthetic. If the text says "synthetic+stress", please read it as "synthetic and transformed-real".
  > - Measured floor ratios at the reference n are 0.967 (gene_expression) to 1.010 (forest), from `floor_ratio_measured`.
  > 
  > **4. Compute.** Per-cell wall seconds in `run_times.csv` sum to 12.76 CPU-h, longest cell 22.1 min. The split is E1 1.56, E3 5.55, E5 1.34, E6 2.80, E7 1.46, E4 0.06.
  > - It includes the disjoint cells (1.08 h, within the 5.6) and the T2 reference cells (exp3t2).
  > - It does **not** include the unclipped re-runs, E9 or the finite-population check. Additional CPU-h:
  >   - E9 sweep: 0.19 (measured, from per-cell `_meta` seconds). `clip_real.csv` is computed from stored cells.
